findings.explanation: google_storage_bucket.bucket.tf:1 was renamed from resource "google_storage_bucket" "bucket" to "pike" (and the IAM binding was updated to match: google_storage_bucket_iam_binding.binding.tf:3), but outputs.tf:4 and outputs.tf:10 still reference google_storage_bucket.bucket. This is a reference to an undeclared resource â€” terraform validate/plan will fail for the root module and both examples that consume it (example/examplea via module.helmrepo, example/exampleb via module.store).
findings.remediation: Update outputs.tf to reference google_storage_bucket.pike instead of google_storage_bucket.bucket in both the "url" and "bucket" outputs.
findings.title: Module outputs reference an undeclared resource after a rename

findings.explanation: variables.tf:148-155 adds a new "kms_key_name" variable with no default and a validation requiring length > 0, making it a required input for any caller of this module. example/examplea/module.helmrepo.tf never sets kms_key_name, so terraform plan/apply for that example will fail with a missing required argument error.
findings.fix:
module "helmrepo" {
  source          = "../../"
  binding_role    = var.binding_role
  binding_members = var.binding_members
  bucket_name     = var.bucket_name
  project         = var.project
  location        = var.location
  log_bucket      = google_storage_bucket.logging.name
  force_destroy   = true
  kms_key_name    = var.kms_key_name
}
findings.remediation: Either pass kms_key_name into the module.helmrepo block (e.g. from a new example variable, mirroring how example/exampleb does it), or give the root variable a safe default so the module remains usable without CMEK.
findings.title: New required module variable kms_key_name is not supplied by example/examplea

findings.explanation: The root module's kms_key_name variable (variables.tf:148-155) validates length(var.kms_key_name) > 0, but example/exampleb/module.store.tf:11 sets kms_key_name = "". This fails validation immediately on plan, so the second example is also broken by the same variable rollout as HOLDEN_BP_002 â€” the two examples are now inconsistent with each other and neither satisfies the new contract.
findings.remediation: Supply a real (or example/test) KMS key resource id for exampleb, e.g. "projects/<project>/locations/global/keyRings/<ring>/cryptoKeys/<key>", consistent with the literal used in example/examplea/google_storage_bucket.logging.tf:9.
findings.title: example/exampleb passes an empty kms_key_name that fails the module's own validation

findings.explanation: variables.tf:43-51 describes binding_role as "Empty = no binding" and defaults it to "", but google_storage_bucket_iam_binding.binding.tf creates the google_storage_bucket_iam_binding.pike resource unconditionally with no count/for_each guard. A caller relying on the documented default (omit binding_role/binding_members) will have Terraform attempt to create an IAM binding with an empty role, which the GCP provider will reject.
findings.fix:
resource "google_storage_bucket_iam_binding" "pike" {
  # checkov:skip=CKV_GCP_28
  count   = var.binding_role == "" ? 0 : 1
  bucket  = google_storage_bucket.pike.name
  role    = var.binding_role
  members = var.binding_members
}
findings.remediation: Guard the IAM binding resource with count = var.binding_role == "" ? 0 : 1 so the documented "empty = no binding" behavior actually holds.
findings.title: "Empty binding_role = no binding" is documented but not implemented

findings.explanation: Every other bucket setting in this module (versioning, force_destroy, lifecycle, website, cors, logging, public access) is parameterised via a variable, but requester_pays = false is hardcoded, making it impossible for a consumer to enable requester-pays without forking the module.
findings.remediation: Add a requester_pays variable (default false) and reference it, for consistency with the rest of the module's configuration surface.
findings.title: requester_pays is hardcoded instead of exposed as a variable
